I've read before that washing your beard regularly with soap/shampoo/conditioner is a bad idea because you wash away the natural oils that your skin produces.

How true is this? If so is that why it's suggested to use beard oils to compensate?

I'm currently only using shampoo/conditioner about once a week, most other days I just rinse it unless I get something gross in it (barbeque) and that's the only day I tend to oil it (right after the shower).

I have to wash more often by necessity. If I don't use a coal tar shampoo at least 3 days a week I get psoriasis. So usually its wash and condition Mon, Wed, Fri and then on Saturday I hit it with neutragena anti residue shampoo to get all the buildup out. I will oil it every day. So far it seems to work fine for me

Granted my beard is shorter at the moment(the past few months) but I mainly wash with cold water and go by feel on what to do next. If my face or beard feel overly oily then I use a facial cleanser on my skin, after that I use coconut oil to prevent dryness and to give it a slight shine. I started using coconut oil after my skin was becoming ridiculously dry when I first started growing because I was shampooing or conditioning multiple times a week.

I think it all depends on what you put in your beard afterwards. Personally what I do is a shampoo and condition every day, but I also oil everyday as well. It's getting to the point as well were the mornings I won't wash, but rather just wax, then in the evening I'll shampoo and condition, and put beard oil in. Last year I had a good sized beard, didn't really follow the same pattern, didn't wash it that often, and it was often very frizzy and homeless looking. This year I've used a lot more product to clean and condition and it's very well managed.

I think it just comes down to the person. I personally have a very oily face and often need to wash it every day due to this. The beard oil helps with moisturizing after drying it out every time.

I treat my beard like the hair on my head. I don't over wash, ever. I use oils and balms. These are nice not only for your beard but also the skin underneath. I've used Honest Amish balm, Grave Before Shave oil, and Dream Beard oil. I also have used Grandpa's Soap for when I'm in the shower. I used the soap in place of shampoos sometimes. I always felt that my beard was very soft after using the soap and after I dried off I would use either an oil or my balm. Beard on!

This song has a different meaning for me. I feel that many associate it with a lost love or a longing for a special someone. For me the lyrics speak to me in a whole different dimension.

I left school after Yr 10 and entered the workforce, I had a shaky end of school and combined a move out of home with the end of my education. I didn't speak to my family for 2 years or so.

In the 4 years after I left school I managed to work myself into a respectable job. I had a few relationships that ended too soon because what I wanted from life just never seemed to line up with my partners.

At one stage I was living 1200km from my family, after I had made amends with my parents. I was working a job that I loved and was seeing a girl who I was enamoured with. Unfortunately, her past crept out of the shadows and it was enough to turn me on my heel and nope out of that relationship. It was very sudden for me and I didn't have the tools to cope with it.

I planned my move and ended up closer to my family and my high school mates. I moved to a little country town and got myself a job with the same company I had been working for when I lived interstate. Life was good, until I was introduced to synthetic pot. I worked a job that required drug testing and as a result I had never been tempted with drugs before. This was a window for me to try something different.

It was a bad choice, I got ridiculously hooked. I spent thousands of dollars, sometimes a few hundred a week. It was relentless. In the end it led to me losing my job, one I wanted to do for 40 years.

For me, the lyrics are the embodiment of present me's desire to wind back the clock and undo my bad decisions. To be in my old house, my old life, my old shoes. To have another go at what I was doing right for so long yet lost sight of the target.

In a room full of emptiness

By a freeway I confess

I was lost in the pages of a book full of death;

These lines embody how I felt in the crux of my addiction. Surrounded by a shallow emptiness that ate away at me. The only thing that brought me relief was also my undoing, my slow death.

Reading how we'll die alone.

And if we're good we'll lay to rest,

Anywhere we want to go.

I truly felt alone, stuck in a place of no return. Part of me convinced myself that there was no harm in what I was doing as it didn't affect others. Little did I know that it was affecting others, probably because I hid away in my shell.

In your house I long to be;

Room by room patiently,

I'll wait for you there like a stone.

I'll wait for you there alone.

My desire to be living the life of past me. In his place I dreamt of being. I would dream of being at his house, sitting on the couch, waiting for successful me to come home so I could share the happiness that was his life.

And on my deathbed I will pray to the gods and the angels,

Like a pagan to anyone who will take me to heaven;

When I used to black out, when I was lost with my thought alone and no body to control, I longed for a release from the prison I had built around myself. I would have turned to anything to achieve otherworldly forgiveness for the bad decisions I had made. Again, I felt like I had done nothing wrong since I believed my actions only affected myself so I deserved to be forgiven, right?

To a place I recall, I was there so long ago.

The sky was bruised, the wine was bled, and there you led me on.

In a world that I now desired, what led to my heavy use was my own perception that my life was somehow not on track. I had fallen into a hole where I felt I missed my youth. I was young 20's and had missed every milestone of my friends' birthdays. I'd missed weddings and births. I had a mate with a 6yo kid who I had never seen. I imagined myself to have been a failure when in actual fact I was doing pretty good. My 'sky was bruised' in the sense that it felt damaged, yet little did I realise it was merely a bump and would heal with time. 'The wine was bled' to me symbolises that I felt drained of life, of my youth. I had been bled dry of whatever it is that was missing. I didn't know what it was but there was something that I had lost over the years.

And on I read until the day was gone;

And I sat in regret of all the things I've done;

I would sit at my computer punching cones, playing games and generally getting nothing done. Before I knew it days has passed. Entire weekends felt like hours, weeks felt like days. A month could pass without me talking to anyone and I didn't think it was strange. Any time I didn't have immediate access to relief I regretted the time I had wasted which in turn made me want to forget that I had wasted that time and always ended in making a call.

For all that I've blessed, and all that I've wronged.

In dreams until my death I will wander on.

My entire life had led me to this point. Every action and decision. Every word spoken, look made, curse uttered. Every breath, every step, every fall. I had been in a good place once but not any more. I felt I had wronged myself, yet in reality I had wronged all those close to me.

I can't really tl;dr this unfortunately, I wouldn't know where to start. The first time I heard this song it tore at my soul. It embodied a lot of what I was thinking but couldn't put together. It helped me sort things out in my life, to square things up and address issues for what they really were. I guess it made me man up, admit responsibility for the decisions that led me to where I was and to start addressing them. I am now on a clean path. I've been clear for a few months and am intermittently attending NA meetings when I feel the need to talk without being judged. I'm working towards bettering my health and towards a career that will be fulfilling. I've got a long way to go but I am taking each step one at a time.

Sorry to bore you with this if you got this far. I hope you enjoyed the song.
